name: Elmen
kurzbeschreibung: Original village in the Lechtal valley, surrounded by untouched nature and secluded hiking trails through the Lechtaler Alpen.
title: Elmen
metaDescription: Elmen in the Lech Valley: Naturpark Tiroler Lech, Klimmbrücke nature park center, Europe's largest lady's slipper orchid reserve in Martinau and Hahntennjoch.
text:
Overview

Elmen is situated at an elevation of 976 meters in the upper Lech Valley in the district of Reutte, right where the rushing Streimbach brook and the Bschlaber Valley merge into the River Lech. Home to approximately 400 residents, this peaceful municipality consists of the main village of Elmen alongside the hamlets of Martinau and Klimm. Framed by commanding peaks of the Lechtal Alps including Elmer Kreuzspitze (2,480 m) and Klimmspitze, Elmen is nestled at the core of the Tiroler Lech Nature Park. Renowned for its braided gravel banks and pristine riparian woodlands, the village offers a tranquil haven for nature lovers far removed from mass tourism.

History

Originating as a high-medieval clearing settlement, Elmen was first documented in 1312 under a name denoting a riverside meadow covered with elm trees. A celebrated local legend dates back to the Thirty Years' War in 1632: while local men defended mountain passes elsewhere against approaching Swedish forces, the resourceful women of Elmen dressed wooden haystacks in coats and hats on the slopes and lit campfires. Tricked into believing a massive army awaited them, the enemy troops retreated without a fight; in remembrance, local women retain the ancient privilege of receiving communion before the men in church. The parish church of the Epiphany originated from a chapel consecrated in 1444 and was refurbished in baroque style following a fire in 1667. The sturdy northern tower retains a fifteenth-century Gothic core, housing an ornate baroque high altar and ceiling frescoes by Joseph Anton Köpfle from 1801.

Getting There

By automobile from Germany, Elmen is accessed toll-free year-round via motorway A7 through Füssen and Reutte along the scenic B198 Lechtal highway. From Vorarlberg, route B198 leads through Warth and the Bregenzerwald into the valley. During summer months, motorists traveling from Innsbruck or Imst can cross the high-alpine Hahntennjoch pass along road L246 directly into Elmen. Rail travelers arrive at Reutte in Tirol station or Füssen terminus. From Reutte railway station, VVT regional bus line 110 runs frequent scheduled services to Elmen. In summer, bus line 155 provides additional direct connections across the Hahntennjoch from Imst. Holders of the Lechtal Aktiv Card benefit from free or discounted regional bus transport.

Tips

A striking attraction is the Klimmbrücke Nature Park Visitor Centre, uniquely constructed spanning the River Lech itself, featuring the interactive wildlife exhibition The Last Wild One. In the hamlet of Martinau lies the largest contiguous lady's slipper orchid habitat in Central Europe, blossoming with thousands of rare yellow orchids from mid-May to mid-June. The long-distance Lechweg trail passes directly through Elmen, inviting scenic stage hikes. Superb mountain routes lead up to the panoramic Stablalm, celebrated as the balcony of the Lech Valley, or up to the summit of Elmer Kreuzspitze. Exploring the rustic side valley of Bschlabs with its historic wooden chalets in Pfafflar offers an unforgettable glimpse of authentic alpine heritage.
